args.text: When a process description says that an action occurs only if a review or decision is approved, model the approval outcome as a conditional branch and represent the approved outcome's required follow-up actions. If the description requires multiple outcomes or actions to be completed, model them as parallel branches joined by a parallel gateway.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Use a boolean formal conditionExpression on a conditional flow only when the description supports the condition.

args.text: When a description states that an approved decision leads to multiple required follow-up actions before the process can finish, model all of those actions as parallel branches and synchronize them before completion.

result.rule: When the description states that several activities are all required before a later activity or outcome: Model the activities as parallel branches and synchronize all branches with a parallel gateway before the later activity or outcome.

When the description states a sequence of activities or a conditional step followed by a later activity: Connect the activities and any modeled gateways in the stated order with sequence flows, including every described transition.

When the description explicitly orders activities or says that work continues until a stated condition is reached: Model the activities in the stated sequence, and do not represent them as parallel or mutually exclusive branches unless the description explicitly supports concurrency or a decision.

When the description makes completion contingent on both a time-based condition and a separate required activity, without stating that one must precede the other.: Model the time-based wait with an intermediate catch event and the activity as a parallel branch; synchronize the branches with a parallel gateway before completion.

args.text: When a process description states an activity, label the BPMN task concisely with its core action and object, preserving the described meaning without adding incidental detail. Use meaningful event labels that reflect the described start or outcome.

trace.reason: Check existing documented guidance on faithful, concise BPMN labels before proposing a rule.

result.rule: When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.

args.text: When a process description states an activity or event, use concise BPMN labels that faithfully preserve its core action, object, trigger, or outcome without adding details or changing its meaning.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers faithful, concise BPMN labels.

result.rule: When the description gives an activity together with contextual or explanatory details that are not needed to distinguish the activity in its process context: Label the BPMN task with its core action and necessary object, omitting redundant contextual modifiers while preserving details essential to the activity’s meaning.

When the description distinguishes an event or activity by its action, actor, object, recipient, or another meaningful qualifier: Label each BPMN element so that it preserves those stated details without substituting a broader or different meaning.

When the description distinguishes a process trigger, an activity, or an outcome from other stages of the process: Label each BPMN element according to the meaning of its corresponding described trigger, activity, or outcome; do not substitute a different stage or its purpose or result.
When the description specifies an activity’s object, recipient, or other meaningful qualifier: Preserve that qualifier in the BPMN task label rather than replacing it with a broader paraphrase.
